section_1.title: The Fragmented Kingdom: The Problem with Current Notation
section_1.content: Introduce the three mathematical 'siblings' that belong together but use confusingly different notations: Exponents (3²=9), Roots (√9=3), and Logarithms (log₃9=2). Use an animation of a character, 'Leo the Lion', trying to solve three different puzzles that are actually the same shape.
section_1.example: Leo sees 2³=8, ∛8=2, and log₂8=3 as three separate languages. We need a 'Universal Translator'.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Map: The Three Pillars
section_2.content: Briefly review the roles of the Base (the multiplier), the Exponent (how many times), and the Result (the total value). Use a simple 2x2x2 block visual to show how 2³ leads to 8.
section_2.example: Base: 2, Exponent: 3, Result: 8. These are the three vertices of our upcoming triangle.

section_3.title: Introducing the Triangle of Power
section_3.content: Construct a single geometric shape (an equilateral triangle) to replace all three notations. Place the Base at the bottom-left vertex, the Exponent at the top vertex, and the Result at the bottom-right vertex. Explain that the relationship remains fixed regardless of which value is missing.
section_3.example: A triangle with '3' on the bottom-left, '2' at the peak, and '9' on the bottom-right represents the complete relationship: 3²=9.

section_4.title: Operation 1: The Power (Top-Down View)
section_4.content: Demonstrate how to find the 'Result' when the bottom-left (Base) and top (Exponent) are known. Visually, the 'power' flows from the base up through the exponent to reach the result.
section_4.example: Input: Base 5, Exponent 2. Visual: The triangle fills from the left and top to reveal '25' at the bottom-right. (5² = 25)

section_5.title: Operation 2: The Root (Right-to-Left View)
section_5.content: Demonstrate finding the 'Base' when the Result and Exponent are known. In the triangle, this looks like tracing the bottom edge backwards from the right corner. This unifies the 'radical' concept into the triangle structure.
section_5.example: Input: Result 64, Exponent 3. Visual: A question mark appears at the Base vertex. Solving it reveals '4' because 4³ = 64.

section_6.title: Operation 3: The Logarithm (Side-Climb View)
section_6.content: Demonstrate finding the 'Exponent' when the Base and Result are known. This is the 'Logarithm'. Visually, we are asking 'to what height' must the base grow to reach the result.
section_6.example: Input: Base 10, Result 1000. Visual: The 'top' vertex is missing. We find it is '3' because 10³ = 1000. This replaces 'log₁₀1000 = 3'.

section_7.title: Summary: The Unified Harmony
section_7.content: A final animation showing the Triangle of Power rotating, with Leo the Lion easily switching between finding bases, exponents, and results using just one mental map. Emphasize that math is about relationships, not just symbols.
section_7.example: The triangle glows, and the symbols √, log, and ^ merge into the single triangular shape, simplifying the student's cognitive load.

*   **Section 7: Summary: The Unified Harmony**: Animates the rotation and synthesis of the triangle, showing how it simplifies multiple mathematical concepts into one mental model.

*   **Section 6: Operation 3 (The Logarithm)**: Demonstrates solving for the Exponent vertex.

section_1.title: The Fragmented Kingdom: The Problem with Current Notation
section_1.content: Introduce the three mathematical 'siblings' that belong together but use confusingly different notations: Exponents (3²=9), Roots (√9=3), and Logarithms (log₃9=2). Use an animation of a character, 'Leo the Lion', trying to solve three different puzzles that are actually the same shape.
section_1.example: Leo sees 2³=8, ∛8=2, and log₂8=3 as three separate languages. We need a 'Universal Translator'.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Map: The Three Pillars
section_2.content: Briefly review the roles of the Base (the multiplier), the Exponent (how many times), and the Result (the total value). Use a simple 2x2x2 block visual to show how 2³ leads to 8.
section_2.example: Base: 2, Exponent: 3, Result: 8. These are the three vertices of our upcoming triangle.

section_3.title: Introducing the Triangle of Power
section_3.content: Construct a single geometric shape (an equilateral triangle) to replace all three notations. Place the Base at the bottom-left vertex, the Exponent at the top vertex, and the Result at the bottom-right vertex. Explain that the relationship remains fixed regardless of which value is missing.
section_3.example: A triangle with '3' on the bottom-left, '2' at the peak, and '9' on the bottom-right represents the complete relationship: 3²=9.

section_4.title: Operation 1: The Power (Top-Down View)
section_4.content: Demonstrate how to find the 'Result' when the bottom-left (Base) and top (Exponent) are known. Visually, the 'power' flows from the base up through the exponent to reach the result.
section_4.example: Input: Base 5, Exponent 2. Visual: The triangle fills from the left and top to reveal '25' at the bottom-right. (5² = 25)

section_5.title: Operation 2: The Root (Right-to-Left View)
section_5.content: Demonstrate finding the 'Base' when the Result and Exponent are known. In the triangle, this looks like tracing the bottom edge backwards from the right corner. This unifies the 'radical' concept into the triangle structure.
section_5.example: Input: Result 64, Exponent 3. Visual: A question mark appears at the Base vertex. Solving it reveals '4' because 4³ = 64.

section_6.title: Operation 3: The Logarithm (Side-Climb View)
section_6.content: Demonstrate finding the 'Exponent' when the Base and Result are known. This is the 'Logarithm'. Visually, we are asking 'to what height' must the base grow to reach the result.
section_6.example: Input: Base 10, Result 1000. Visual: The 'top' vertex is missing. We find it is '3' because 10³ = 1000. This replaces 'log₁₀1000 = 3'.

section_7.title: Summary: The Unified Harmony
section_7.content: A final animation showing the Triangle of Power rotating, with Leo the Lion easily switching between finding bases, exponents, and results using just one mental map. Emphasize that math is about relationships, not just symbols.
section_7.example: The triangle glows, and the symbols √, log, and ^ merge into the single triangular shape, simplifying the student's cognitive load.

section_1.title: The Fragmented Kingdom: The Problem with Current Notation
lecture_lines: Exponents, roots, and logarithms often feel like separate languages.
But these three operations are actually deeply connected siblings.
Our current notation hides this beautiful mathematical symmetry.
animations: Show '2³=8', '∛8=2', and 'log₂8=3' in different colors (#ADD8E6, #90EE90, #FFB6C1) scattered on screen.
Highlight '2³=8' in the center while other expressions fade slightly.
Highlight '∛8=2' in the center while other expressions fade slightly.
Highlight 'log₂8=3' in the center while other expressions fade slightly.
Character 'Leo' (yellow circle #FFFFE0) appears looking confused by three white puzzle boxes (#FFFFFF).

section_2.title: Prerequisite Map: The Three Pillars
lecture_lines: Every power relationship involves a base and an exponent.
Multiplying the base repeatedly gives us the final result.
These three values form the foundation of our triangle.
animations: Display 'Base: 2' in blue (#0000FF) alongside a single 3D-looking cube.
Display 'Exponent: 3' in green (#00FF00) as the cube multiplies into a 2x2x2 block.
Display 'Result: 8' in red (#FF0000) as a label for the completed 8-cube block.

section_3.title: Introducing the Triangle of Power
lecture_lines: Meet the Triangle of Power: a unified mathematical map.
The base sits at the bottom-left vertex.
The exponent climbs to the top peak.
The final result rests at the bottom-right vertex.
One single shape replaces three different notations.
animations: Draw a white (#FFFFFF) equilateral triangle outline centered on the screen.
Place '3' (Base) at the bottom-left vertex in blue (#0000FF) with a brief glow.
Place '2' (Exponent) at the top vertex in green (#00FF00) with a brief glow.
Place '9' (Result) at the bottom-right vertex in red (#FF0000) with a brief glow.
The entire triangle pulses with a soft white light (#FFFFFF) to show the unified relationship.

section_4.title: Operation 1: The Power (Top-Down View)
lecture_lines: To find a power, look from base to exponent.
Five raised to the power of two equals twenty-five.
The result flows naturally to the bottom-right corner.
animations: Show the triangle with '5' (blue, #0000FF) at bottom-left and '2' (green, #00FF00) at the top vertex.
Animate a yellow glowing arrow (#FFFF00) flowing from the Base and Exponent toward the Result vertex.
Reveal '25' (red, #FF0000) at the bottom-right vertex with a scaling and flash effect.

section_5.title: Operation 2: The Root (Right-to-Left View)
lecture_lines: Finding a root means searching for the missing base.
We move from the result back to the start.
The triangle unifies radicals into this simple structure.
animations: Show the triangle with '64' (red, #FF0000) at bottom-right and '3' (green, #00FF00) at the top vertex.
Animate a yellow glowing line (#FFFF00) tracing back from the Result and Exponent toward the Base vertex.
Reveal '4' (blue, #0000FF) at the bottom-left vertex with a scaling and flash effect.

section_6.title: Operation 3: The Logarithm (Side-Climb View)
lecture_lines: Logarithms ask what exponent connects the base and result.
We climb the side to find the top value.
Ten cubed is one thousand, so the exponent is three.
animations: Show the triangle with '10' (blue, #0000FF) at bottom-left and '1000' (red, #FF0000) at the bottom-right vertex.
Animate a yellow line (#FFFF00) 'climbing' from the bottom edge up to the Exponent peak.
Reveal '3' (green, #00FF00) at the top vertex with a scaling and flash effect.

section_7.title: Summary: The Unified Harmony
lecture_lines: The Triangle of Power reveals the harmony in math.
No more switching between confusing symbols and rules.
One mental map simplifies your mathematical journey.
animations: Rotate the Triangle of Power slowly with numbers 2, 3, and 8 on its vertices.
Flash the vertices in sequence to emphasize looking at the relationship from different angles.
Fade out the traditional symbols √, log, and ^ as they drift away from the triangle.
The triangle edges glow bright white (#FFFFFF) signifying the 'Unified Harmony'.
Leo the Lion (yellow circle, #FFFFE0) appears next to the triangle, jumping happily.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite Map: The Three Pillars", 
            [
                "Every power relationship involves a base and an exponent.",
                "Multiplying the base repeatedly gives us the final result.",
                "These three values form the foundation of our triangle."
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        COLOR_BASE = "#0000FF"    # Blue
        COLOR_EXPONENT = "#00FF00" # Green
        COLOR_RESULT = "#FF0000"   # Red

        def create_pseudo_cube(color, side_length=0.6):
            # 2D representation of a 3D cube
            front = Square(side_length=side_length, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
            
            # Offset for perspective
            offset = side_length * 0.3
            
            top = Polygon(
                front.get_corner(UL), front.get_corner(UR),
                front.get_corner(UR) + [offset, offset, 0],
                front.get_corner(UL) + [offset, offset, 0],
                fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1
            ).set_color(color).lighten(0.3)
            
            right = Polygon(
                front.get_corner(UR), front.get_corner(DR),
                front.get_corner(DR) + [offset, offset, 0],
                front.get_corner(UR) + [offset, offset, 0],
                fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1
            ).set_color(color).darken(0.3)
            
            return VGroup(front, top, right)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        base_label = Text("Base: 2", font_size=24, color=COLOR_BASE)

        self.place_at_grid(single_cube, "B4")
        
        self.play(
            Write(base_label),
            FadeIn(single_cube)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display 'Exponent: 3' in green as the cube multiplies into a 2x2x2 block.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_EXPONENT))
        
        exponent_label = Text("Exponent: 3", font_size=24, color=COLOR_EXPONENT)
        self.place_at_grid(exponent_label, "C2")

        # Create a 2x2x2 block of cubes
        # To handle 2D layering, we draw back-to-front, bottom-to-top, left-to-right
        block_cubes = VGroup()
        side = 0.5
        spacing = side * 1.1 # slightly more than side length to show distinct cubes
        
        # Grid for the block: z=0 is back, z=1 is front
        for z in range(2):
            for y in range(2):
                for x in range(2):
                    c = create_pseudo_cube(COLOR_EXPONENT, side_length=side)
                    # Position relative to a local center, then moved to grid
                    # Note: We simulate 3D offset by shifting based on z
                    offset_3d = z * (side * 0.3)
                    pos = np.array([
                        x * side + offset_3d, 
                        -y * side + offset_3d, 
                        0
                    ])
                    c.move_to(pos)
                    block_cubes.add(c)
        
        # Sort block_cubes to ensure correct draw order (Z-index simulation)
        # In 2D, we just need to add them to the scene in the right order.
        # The loop above already handles back-to-front (z) and bottom-to-top (y inverse)
        
        self.place_in_area(block_cubes, "C4", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            Write(exponent_label),
            ReplacementTransform(single_cube, block_cubes)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display 'Result: 8' in red as a label for the completed 8-cube block.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULT))
        
        result_label = Text("Result: 8", font_size=24, color=COLOR_RESULT)
        self.place_at_grid(result_label, "D2")
        
        # Highlight the block in red
        highlight_rect = SurroundingRectangle(block_cubes, color=COLOR_RESULT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            Write(result_label),
            Create(highlight_rect),
            block_cubes.animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULT)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        )

            "No more switching between confusing symbols and rules.",

        self.setup_layout("Summary: The Unified Harmony", lecture_lines)
        
        # Triangle vertex positions based on grid
        p_base = self.grid["D2"]
        p_exp = (self.grid["B3"] + self.grid["B4"]) / 2

            run_time=4, 
            rate_func=linear
        )

        sym_root = MathTex("\\sqrt[y]{x}", color=GRAY)
        sym_log = MathTex("\\log_x y", color=GRAY)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sym_pow, "A2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(sym_root, "F1", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(sym_log, "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sym_pow), FadeIn(sym_root), FadeIn(sym_log))
        self.wait(1)

            sym_pow.animate.shift(UP * 1.5 + LEFT * 1).set_opacity(0),
            sym_root.animate.shift(LEFT * 1.5 + DOWN * 1).set_opacity(0),
            sym_log.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.5 + DOWN * 1).set_opacity(0),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # One mental map simplifies your mathematical journey.

        self.lecture[2].set_color(CYAN)
        
        # Triangle edges glow bright white (#FFFFFF)

        self.add(glow)
        self.play(

            glow.animate.scale(1.3).set_opacity(0),
            run_time=1.5,
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        self.remove(glow)
        
        # Leo the Lion (yellow circle, #FFFFE0) appears and jumps
        leo = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#FFFFE0", fill_opacity=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(leo, "E1")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(leo))
        
        # Jumping animation
        for _ in range(3):
            self.play(leo.animate.shift(UP * 0.5), run_time=0.3, rate_func=ease_out_sine)
            self.play(leo.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.5), run_time=0.3, rate_func=ease_in_sine)
            
        self.wait(3)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data from storyboard
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Triangle of Power reveals the harmony in math.",
            "No more switching between confusing symbols and rules.",

        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The Unified Harmony", lecture_lines)
        
        # Triangle vertex positions based on grid
        p_base = self.grid["D2"]
        p_exp = (self.grid["B3"] + self.grid["B4"]) / 2
        p_res = self.grid["D5"]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The Triangle of Power reveals the harmony in math.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        triangle = Polygon(p_base, p_exp, p_res, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        val_base = Text("2", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
        val_exp = Text("3", font_size=36, color=RED)
        val_res = Text("8", font_size=36, color=GREEN)
        
        # Positioning labels within 1 grid unit of vertices
        val_base.move_to(p_base + LEFT * 0.4 + DOWN * 0.2)
        val_exp.move_to(p_exp + UP * 0.4)
        val_res.move_to(p_res + RIGHT * 0.4 + DOWN * 0.2)
        
        triangle_group = VGroup(triangle, val_base, val_exp, val_res)
        
        self.play(Create(triangle), Write(val_base), Write(val_exp), Write(val_res))
        
        # Rotate slowly with numbers on vertices
        self.play(
            Rotate(triangle_group, angle=TAU, about_point=triangle.get_center()), 
            run_time=4, 
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        # Flash vertices in sequence to emphasize relationships
        self.play(Flash(p_base, color=BLUE, flash_radius=0.5))
        self.play(Flash(p_exp, color=RED, flash_radius=0.5))
        self.play(Flash(p_res, color=GREEN, flash_radius=0.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # No more switching between confusing symbols and rules.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        # Traditional symbols to fade out

        self.place_at_grid(sym_pow, "A2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(sym_root, "F1", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(sym_log, "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sym_pow), FadeIn(sym_root), FadeIn(sym_log))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Symbols drift away and fade out
        self.play(
            sym_pow.animate.shift(UP * 1.5 + LEFT * 1).set_opacity(0),
            sym_root.animate.shift(LEFT * 1.5 + DOWN * 1).set_opacity(0),
            sym_log.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.5 + DOWN * 1).set_opacity(0),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # One mental map simplifies your mathematical journey.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(CYAN)
        
        # Triangle edges glow bright white (#FFFFFF)
        glow = triangle.copy().set_stroke(WHITE, width=12, opacity=0.6)
        self.add(glow)
        self.play(

            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        self.remove(glow)
        
        # Leo the Lion (yellow circle, #FFFFE0) appears and jumps

        self.wait(3)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

section_1.title: The Fragmented Kingdom: The Problem with Current Notation
section_1.content: Introduce the three mathematical 'siblings' that belong together but use confusingly different notations: Exponents (3²=9), Roots (√9=3), and Logarithms (log₃9=2). Use an animation of a character, 'Leo the Lion', trying to solve three different puzzles that are actually the same shape.
section_1.example: Leo sees 2³=8, ∛8=2, and log₂8=3 as three separate languages. We need a 'Universal Translator'.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Map: The Three Pillars
section_2.content: Briefly review the roles of the Base (the multiplier), the Exponent (how many times), and the Result (the total value). Use a simple 2x2x2 block visual to show how 2³ leads to 8.
section_2.example: Base: 2, Exponent: 3, Result: 8. These are the three vertices of our upcoming triangle.

section_3.title: Introducing the Triangle of Power
section_3.content: Construct a single geometric shape (an equilateral triangle) to replace all three notations. Place the Base at the bottom-left vertex, the Exponent at the top vertex, and the Result at the bottom-right vertex. Explain that the relationship remains fixed regardless of which value is missing.
section_3.example: A triangle with '3' on the bottom-left, '2' at the peak, and '9' on the bottom-right represents the complete relationship: 3²=9.

section_4.title: Operation 1: The Power (Top-Down View)
section_4.content: Demonstrate how to find the 'Result' when the bottom-left (Base) and top (Exponent) are known. Visually, the 'power' flows from the base up through the exponent to reach the result.
section_4.example: Input: Base 5, Exponent 2. Visual: The triangle fills from the left and top to reveal '25' at the bottom-right. (5² = 25)

section_5.title: Operation 2: The Root (Right-to-Left View)
section_5.content: Demonstrate finding the 'Base' when the Result and Exponent are known. In the triangle, this looks like tracing the bottom edge backwards from the right corner. This unifies the 'radical' concept into the triangle structure.
section_5.example: Input: Result 64, Exponent 3. Visual: A question mark appears at the Base vertex. Solving it reveals '4' because 4³ = 64.

section_6.title: Operation 3: The Logarithm (Side-Climb View)
section_6.content: Demonstrate finding the 'Exponent' when the Base and Result are known. This is the 'Logarithm'. Visually, we are asking 'to what height' must the base grow to reach the result.
section_6.example: Input: Base 10, Result 1000. Visual: The 'top' vertex is missing. We find it is '3' because 10³ = 1000. This replaces 'log₁₀1000 = 3'.

section_7.title: Summary: The Unified Harmony
section_7.content: A final animation showing the Triangle of Power rotating, with Leo the Lion easily switching between finding bases, exponents, and results using just one mental map. Emphasize that math is about relationships, not just symbols.
section_7.example: The triangle glows, and the symbols √, log, and ^ merge into the single triangular shape, simplifying the student's cognitive load.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Fragmented Kingdom: The Problem with Current Notation"
        lines = [
            "- Exponents, roots, and logarithms often feel like separate languages.",
            "- But these three operations are actually deeply connected siblings.",
            "- Our current notation hides this beautiful mathematical symmetry."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors from storyboard
        color_exp = "#ADD8E6"  # Light Blue
        color_root = "#90EE90" # Light Green
        color_log = "#FFB6C1"  # Light Pink
        color_leo = "#FFFFE0"  # Light Yellow
        color_puzzle = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show '2³=8', '∛8=2', and 'log₂8=3' scattered
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        exp_eq = MathTex("2^3=8", color=color_exp)
        root_eq = MathTex("\\sqrt[3]{8}=2", color=color_root)
        log_eq = MathTex("\\log_2 8=3", color=color_log)
        
        self.place_at_grid(exp_eq, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(root_eq, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(log_eq, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(exp_eq), FadeIn(root_eq), FadeIn(log_eq))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight each expression in the center while others fade
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Define a center for highlighting
        center_mobj = VMobject()
        self.place_in_area(center_mobj, "B3", "E4")
        center_pos = center_mobj.get_center()
        
        # Highlight exp
        self.play(
            exp_eq.animate.move_to(center_pos).scale(1.5),
            root_eq.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            log_eq.animate.set_opacity(0.3)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Highlight root
        self.play(
            exp_eq.animate.move_to(self.grid["B2"]).scale(1/1.5).set_opacity(0.3),
            root_eq.animate.move_to(center_pos).scale(1.5).set_opacity(1),
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Highlight log
        self.play(
            root_eq.animate.move_to(self.grid["D4"]).scale(1/1.5).set_opacity(0.3),
            log_eq.animate.move_to(center_pos).scale(1.5).set_opacity(1),
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Return log to its place
        self.play(
            log_eq.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]).scale(1/1.5).set_opacity(0.3)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Character 'Leo' and puzzle boxes
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            FadeOut(exp_eq), FadeOut(root_eq), FadeOut(log_eq)
        )
        
        # Leo character (represented as a yellow circle)
        leo = Circle(radius=0.5, color=color_leo, fill_opacity=1)
        leo_label = Text("Leo", font_size=18, color=color_leo)
        self.place_at_grid(leo, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        leo_label.next_to(leo, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # Puzzle boxes (white squares)
        box1 = Square(side_length=0.7, color=color_puzzle)
        box2 = Square(side_length=0.7, color=color_puzzle)
        box3 = Square(side_length=0.7, color=color_puzzle)
        
        self.place_at_grid(box1, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(box2, "C5")
        self.place_at_grid(box3, "E4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(leo), FadeIn(leo_label))
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                Create(box1), Create(box2), Create(box3),
                lag_ratio=0.3
            )
        )
        
        # Leo's confusion (question marks)
        q1 = Text("?", color=color_leo).scale(0.8)
        q2 = Text("?", color=color_leo).scale(0.8)
        q3 = Text("?", color=color_leo).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(q1, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(q2, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(q3, "E2")
        
        self.play(Write(q1), Write(q2), Write(q3))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite Map: The Three Pillars", 
            [
                "Every power relationship involves a base and an exponent.",
                "Multiplying the base repeatedly gives us the final result.",
                "These three values form the foundation of our triangle."
            ]
        )

        # Colors - Using ManimColor to ensure compatibility with interpolate_color
        COLOR_BASE = ManimColor("#0000FF")    # Blue
        COLOR_EXPONENT = ManimColor("#00FF00") # Green
        COLOR_RESULT = ManimColor("#FF0000")   # Red

        def create_pseudo_cube(color, side_length=0.6):
            # Ensure the color is a ManimColor object so that .interpolate() can be called
            m_color = ManimColor(color)
            
            # 2D representation of a 3D cube
            front = Square(side_length=side_length, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=m_color, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
            
            # Offset for perspective
            offset = side_length * 0.3
            
            # Use interpolate_color on ManimColor objects
            color_light = interpolate_color(m_color, WHITE, 0.3)
            color_dark = interpolate_color(m_color, BLACK, 0.3)

            top = Polygon(
                front.get_corner(UL), front.get_corner(UR),
                front.get_corner(UR) + [offset, offset, 0],
                front.get_corner(UL) + [offset, offset, 0],
                fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color_light, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1
            )
            
            right = Polygon(
                front.get_corner(UR), front.get_corner(DR),
                front.get_corner(DR) + [offset, offset, 0],
                front.get_corner(UR) + [offset, offset, 0],
                fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color_dark, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1
            )
            
            return VGroup(front, top, right)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_BASE))
        
        base_label = Text("Base: 2", font_size=24, color=COLOR_BASE)
        self.place_at_grid(base_label, "B2")
        
        single_cube = create_pseudo_cube(COLOR_BASE)
        self.place_at_grid(single_cube, "B4")
        
        self.play(
            Write(base_label),
            FadeIn(single_cube)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_EXPONENT))
        
        exponent_label = Text("Exponent: 3", font_size=24, color=COLOR_EXPONENT)
        self.place_at_grid(exponent_label, "C2")

        # Create a 2x2x2 block of cubes
        block_cubes = VGroup()
        side = 0.5
        
        for z in range(2): # Back to front
            for y in range(2): # Top to bottom
                for x in range(2): # Left to right
                    c = create_pseudo_cube(COLOR_EXPONENT, side_length=side)
                    offset_3d = z * (side * 0.3)
                    pos = np.array([
                        x * side + offset_3d, 
                        -y * side + offset_3d, 
                        0
                    ])
                    c.move_to(pos)
                    block_cubes.add(c)
        
        self.place_in_area(block_cubes, "C4", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            Write(exponent_label),
            ReplacementTransform(single_cube, block_cubes)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULT))
        
        result_label = Text("Result: 8", font_size=24, color=COLOR_RESULT)
        self.place_at_grid(result_label, "D2")
        
        # Highlight the block in red
        highlight_rect = SurroundingRectangle(block_cubes, color=COLOR_RESULT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            Write(result_label),
            Create(highlight_rect),
            block_cubes.animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULT)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Lecture Data
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Triangle of Power reveals the harmony in math.",
            "No more switching between confusing symbols and rules.",
            "One mental map simplifies your mathematical journey."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The Unified Harmony", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid positions for the Triangle
        p_base = self.grid["D2"]
        p_exp = (self.grid["B3"] + self.grid["B4"]) / 2
        p_res = self.grid["D5"]
        
        # --- Animation for Line 1 ---
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        triangle = Polygon(p_base, p_exp, p_res, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        val_base = Text("2", font_size=32, color=BLUE)
        val_exp = Text("3", font_size=32, color=RED)
        val_res = Text("8", font_size=32, color=GREEN)
        
        # Position labels near vertices
        val_base.move_to(p_base + LEFT * 0.5 + DOWN * 0.3)
        val_exp.move_to(p_exp + UP * 0.5)
        val_res.move_to(p_res + RIGHT * 0.5 + DOWN * 0.3)
        
        triangle_group = VGroup(triangle, val_base, val_exp, val_res)
        
        self.play(Create(triangle), Write(val_base), Write(val_exp), Write(val_res))
        self.play(
            Rotate(triangle_group, angle=TAU, about_point=triangle.get_center()),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        self.play(Flash(p_base, color=BLUE), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(Flash(p_exp, color=RED), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(Flash(p_res, color=GREEN), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # --- Animation for Line 2 ---
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        # Traditional notation drifting and fading
        sym_pow = MathTex("x^y", color=GRAY)
        sym_root = MathTex("\\sqrt[y]{x}", color=GRAY)
        sym_log = MathTex("\\log_x y", color=GRAY)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sym_pow, "A2", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(sym_root, "F1", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(sym_log, "F6", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sym_pow), FadeIn(sym_root), FadeIn(sym_log))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(
            sym_pow.animate.shift(UP * 1.5 + LEFT * 1).set_opacity(0),
            sym_root.animate.shift(LEFT * 1.5 + DOWN * 1).set_opacity(0),
            sym_log.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.5 + DOWN * 1).set_opacity(0),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # --- Animation for Line 3 ---
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(TEAL)
        
        # Glowing effect for Triangle
        glow = triangle.copy().set_stroke(WHITE, width=15, opacity=0.8)
        self.play(
            triangle.animate.set_stroke(WHITE, width=10),
            FadeIn(glow),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            glow.animate.scale(1.4).set_opacity(0),
            run_time=1.0,
            rate_func=rate_functions.ease_out_quad
        )
        self.remove(glow)
        
        # Character "Leo" (Circle)
        leo = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FFFFE0", fill_opacity=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(leo, "E1")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(leo))
        
        # Jumping across the scene
        for _ in range(3):
            self.play(leo.animate.shift(UP * 0.6), run_time=0.3, rate_func=rate_functions.ease_out_sine)
            self.play(leo.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.6), run_time=0.3, rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_sine)
            
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite Map: The Three Pillars", 
            [
                "Every power relationship involves a base and an exponent.",
                "Multiplying the base repeatedly gives us the final result.",
                "These three values form the foundation of our triangle."
            ]
        )

        # Colors - Using ManimColor to ensure compatibility with interpolate_color
        COLOR_BASE = ManimColor("#0000FF")    # Blue
        COLOR_EXPONENT = ManimColor("#00FF00") # Green
        COLOR_RESULT = ManimColor("#FF0000")   # Red

        def create_pseudo_cube(color, side_length=0.6):
            # Ensure the color is a ManimColor object so that .interpolate() can be called
            m_color = ManimColor(color)
            
            # 2D representation of a 3D cube
            front = Square(side_length=side_length, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=m_color, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
            
            # Offset for perspective
            offset = side_length * 0.3
            
            # Use interpolate_color on ManimColor objects
            color_light = interpolate_color(m_color, WHITE, 0.3)
            color_dark = interpolate_color(m_color, BLACK, 0.3)

            top = Polygon(
                front.get_corner(UL), front.get_corner(UR),
                front.get_corner(UR) + [offset, offset, 0],
                front.get_corner(UL) + [offset, offset, 0],
                fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color_light, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1
            )
            
            right = Polygon(
                front.get_corner(UR), front.get_corner(DR),
                front.get_corner(DR) + [offset, offset, 0],
                front.get_corner(UR) + [offset, offset, 0],
                fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color_dark, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1
            )
            
            return VGroup(front, top, right)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_BASE))
        
        base_label = Text("Base: 2", font_size=24, color=COLOR_BASE)
        self.place_at_grid(base_label, "B2")
        
        single_cube = create_pseudo_cube(COLOR_BASE)
        self.place_at_grid(single_cube, "B4")
        
        self.play(
            Write(base_label),
            FadeIn(single_cube)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_EXPONENT))
        
        exponent_label = Text("Exponent: 3", font_size=24, color=COLOR_EXPONENT)
        self.place_at_grid(exponent_label, "C2")

        # Create a 2x2x2 block of cubes
        block_cubes = VGroup()
        side = 0.5
        
        for z in range(2): # Back to front
            for y in range(2): # Top to bottom
                for x in range(2): # Left to right
                    c = create_pseudo_cube(COLOR_EXPONENT, side_length=side)
                    offset_3d = z * (side * 0.3)
                    pos = np.array([
                        x * side + offset_3d, 
                        -y * side + offset_3d, 
                        0
                    ])
                    c.move_to(pos)
                    block_cubes.add(c)
        
        self.place_in_area(block_cubes, "C4", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            Write(exponent_label),
            ReplacementTransform(single_cube, block_cubes)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULT))
        
        result_label = Text("Result: 8", font_size=24, color=COLOR_RESULT)
        self.place_at_grid(result_label, "D2")
        
        # Highlight the block in red
        highlight_rect = SurroundingRectangle(block_cubes, color=COLOR_RESULT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            Write(result_label),
            Create(highlight_rect),
            block_cubes.animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULT)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_str = "Operation 2: The Root (Right-to-Left View)"
        lines_str = [
            "- Finding a root means searching for the missing base.",
            "- We move from the result back to the start.",
            "- The triangle unifies radicals into this simple structure."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines_str)

        # Triangle vertices
        base_pos = self.grid["E2"]
        result_pos = self.grid["E6"]
        exponent_pos = self.grid["B4"]

        # Triangle lines
        side_left = Line(base_pos, exponent_pos, color=GRAY)
        side_right = Line(exponent_pos, result_pos, color=GRAY)
        side_bottom = Line(result_pos, base_pos, color=GRAY)
        triangle = VGroup(side_left, side_right, side_bottom)

        # Mobjects for values
        val_64 = Text("64", color="#FF0000", font_size=36)
        val_3 = Text("3", color="#00FF00", font_size=36)
        val_4 = Text("4", color="#0000FF", font_size=36)
        val_question = Text("?", color=WHITE, font_size=36)

        # Position values
        self.place_at_grid(val_64, "E6")
        self.place_at_grid(val_3, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(val_4, "E2")
        self.place_at_grid(val_question, "E2")

        # Labels for vertices
        lbl_res = Text("Result", font_size=18).next_to(val_64, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        lbl_exp = Text("Exponent", font_size=18).next_to(val_3, UP, buff=0.2)
        lbl_base = Text("Base", font_size=18).next_to(val_question, DOWN, buff=0.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Finding a root means searching for the missing base.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(
            Create(triangle),
            Write(val_64),
            Write(val_3),
            Write(val_question),
            Write(lbl_res),
            Write(lbl_exp),
            Write(lbl_base),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # We move from the result back to the start.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )

        # Yellow glowing lines tracing back
        trace_bottom = Line(result_pos, base_pos, color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=6)
        trace_top = Line(exponent_pos, base_pos, color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=6)
        
        self.play(

outline.title: The Fragmented Kingdom: The Problem with Current Notation
outline.content: Introduce the three mathematical 'siblings' that belong together but use confusingly different notations: Exponents (3²=9), Roots (√9=3), and Logarithms (log₃9=2). Use an animation of a character, 'Leo the Lion', trying to solve three different puzzles that are actually the same shape.
outline.example: Leo sees 2³=8, ∛8=2, and log₂8=3 as three separate languages. We need a 'Universal Translator'.

storyboard.title: The Fragmented Kingdom: The Problem with Current Notation
lecture_lines: Exponents, roots, and logarithms often feel like separate languages.
But these three operations are actually deeply connected siblings.
Our current notation hides this beautiful mathematical symmetry.
animations: Show '2³=8', '∛8=2', and 'log₂8=3' in different colors (#ADD8E6, #90EE90, #FFB6C1) scattered on screen.
Highlight '2³=8' in the center while other expressions fade slightly.
Highlight '∛8=2' in the center while other expressions fade slightly.
Highlight 'log₂8=3' in the center while other expressions fade slightly.
Character 'Leo' (yellow circle #FFFFE0) appears looking confused by three white puzzle boxes (#FFFFFF).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Fragmented Kingdom: The Problem with Current Notation"
        lines = [
            "- Exponents, roots, and logarithms often feel like separate languages.",
            "- But these three operations are actually deeply connected siblings.",
            "- Our current notation hides this beautiful mathematical symmetry."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors from storyboard
        color_exp = "#ADD8E6"  # Light Blue
        color_root = "#90EE90" # Light Green
        color_log = "#FFB6C1"  # Light Pink
        color_leo = "#FFFFE0"  # Light Yellow
        color_puzzle = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show '2³=8', '∛8=2', and 'log₂8=3' scattered
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        exp_eq = MathTex("2^3=8", color=color_exp)
        root_eq = MathTex("\\sqrt[3]{8}=2", color=color_root)
        log_eq = MathTex("\\log_2 8=3", color=color_log)
        
        self.place_at_grid(exp_eq, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(root_eq, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(log_eq, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(exp_eq), FadeIn(root_eq), FadeIn(log_eq))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight each expression in the center while others fade
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Define a center for highlighting
        center_mobj = VMobject()
        self.place_in_area(center_mobj, "B3", "E4")
        center_pos = center_mobj.get_center()
        
        # Highlight exp
        self.play(
            exp_eq.animate.move_to(center_pos).scale(1.5),
            root_eq.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            log_eq.animate.set_opacity(0.3)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Highlight root
        self.play(
            exp_eq.animate.move_to(self.grid["B2"]).scale(1/1.5).set_opacity(0.3),
            root_eq.animate.move_to(center_pos).scale(1.5).set_opacity(1),
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Highlight log
        self.play(
            root_eq.animate.move_to(self.grid["D4"]).scale(1/1.5).set_opacity(0.3),
            log_eq.animate.move_to(center_pos).scale(1.5).set_opacity(1),
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Return log to its place
        self.play(
            log_eq.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]).scale(1/1.5).set_opacity(0.3)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Character 'Leo' and puzzle boxes
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            FadeOut(exp_eq), FadeOut(root_eq), FadeOut(log_eq)
        )
        
        # Leo character (represented as a yellow circle)
        leo = Circle(radius=0.5, color=color_leo, fill_opacity=1)
        leo_label = Text("Leo", font_size=18, color=color_leo)
        self.place_at_grid(leo, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        leo_label.next_to(leo, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # Puzzle boxes (white squares)
        box1 = Square(side_length=0.7, color=color_puzzle)
        box2 = Square(side_length=0.7, color=color_puzzle)
        box3 = Square(side_length=0.7, color=color_puzzle)
        
        self.place_at_grid(box1, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(box2, "C5")
        self.place_at_grid(box3, "E4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(leo), FadeIn(leo_label))
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                Create(box1), Create(box2), Create(box3),
                lag_ratio=0.3
            )
        )
        
        # Leo's confusion (question marks)
        q1 = Text("?", color=color_leo).scale(0.8)
        q2 = Text("?", color=color_leo).scale(0.8)
        q3 = Text("?", color=color_leo).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(q1, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(q2, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(q3, "E2")
        
        self.play(Write(q1), Write(q2), Write(q3))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Operation 3: The Logarithm (Side-Climb View)
outline.content: Demonstrate finding the 'Exponent' when the Base and Result are known. This is the 'Logarithm'. Visually, we are asking 'to what height' must the base grow to reach the result.
outline.example: Input: Base 10, Result 1000. Visual: The 'top' vertex is missing. We find it is '3' because 10³ = 1000. This replaces 'log₁₀1000 = 3'.

storyboard.title: Operation 3: The Logarithm (Side-Climb View)
lecture_lines: Logarithms ask what exponent connects the base and result.
We climb the side to find the top value.
